problem_motivation.content: Need to develop and design new alloy materials with lightweight and superior comprehensive performance.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: To develop and design new alloy materials with lightweight and superior comprehensive performance.

problem_motivation.content: Performance improvements in traditional alloys are limited, creating a need to meet stringent demands for comprehensive material properties in cutting-edge equipment.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: the room for improving the performance of traditional alloys has become increasingly limited, making it difficult to meet the ever more stringent demands for comprehensive material properties in cutting-edge equipment

problem_motivation.content: There is a significant gap in understanding the microstructural evolution and functional properties of magnesium-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: While research on magnesium-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys (Mg-containing LWHEAs) has made initial progress, significant limitations remain in understanding their microstructural evolution and functional properties

prior_approach.content: Previous studies have prepared various lightweight high-entropy alloys using induction melting and investigated their properties.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Shao et al. [ [12] ] prepared six kinds of lightweight high-entropy alloys rich in Al and Mg elements using induction melting

prior_approach.content: Tseng et al. designed a specific Al20Be20Fe10Si15Ti35 lightweight high-entropy alloy with low density and high hardness.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The Al 20 Be 20 Fe 10 Si 15 Ti 35 lightweight high-entropy alloy designed by Tseng et al. [ [13] ] has a density of only 3.91 g/cm 3 but a hardness as high as 911 HV

prior_approach.content: Yao et al. employed high-throughput gradient continuous casting to prepare a compositionally graded MgAlCuZnGd alloy.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Yao et al. [ [14] ] employed high-throughput gradient continuous casting technology to prepare a compositionally graded MgAlCuZnGd lightweight high-entropy alloy

prior_approach.content: Satya et al. fabricated AlMgₓTiSnZn alloys via mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering to investigate their properties.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Satya et al. [ [15] ] successfully fabricated AlMgₓTiSnZn (x = 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5) lightweight high-entropy alloys via mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering

prior_limitation.content: The phase transformation pathways, precipitation sequences, and kinetic mechanisms of metastable solid solution phases under non-equilibrium conditions remain unclear.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: the subsequent phase transformation pathways, precipitation sequences, and kinetic mechanisms of metastable solid solution phases under non-equilibrium processing conditions are not yet clear

prior_limitation.content: There is a lack of systematic studies and integrated atomic-scale experiments and simulations regarding segregation behavior, interfacial energy, and diffusion characteristics.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: systematic studies are lacking on the segregation behavior, interfacial energy, and diffusion characteristics of light elements and transition metals at interfaces, with a particular shortage of integrated atomic-scale experiments and simulations

prior_limitation.content: Existing research has focused primarily on mechanical properties, leaving high-temperature oxidation resistance and corrosion resistance relatively under-studied.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: existing work has primarily focused on fundamental mechanical properties such as hardness and room-temperature compression, while research on microstructural evolution laws and key functional properties like high-temperature oxidation resistance and corrosion resistance remains relatively scarce

prior_limitation.content: Significant differences in atomic properties between magnesium and other elements lead to stable intermetallic compounds, constraining performance optimization.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: the significant differences in atomic radius, electronegativity, and other properties between magnesium and other constituent elements often lead to the formation of stable intermetallic compounds, further constraining the optimization of material performance

prior_limitation.content: Completely avoiding oxygen introduction during prolonged high-energy mechanical alloying remains highly challenging.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Nevertheless, completely avoiding oxygen introduction during prolonged high-energy mechanical alloying remains highly challenging.

causal_claim.content: Sintering at 1000 °C resulted in high densification (96.7%) and high microhardness (1235.5 HV).
causal_claim.evidence_span: When the sintering temperature reached 1000 °C, the alloy achieved a densification of 96.7% and a microhardness of 1235.5 HV.

causal_claim.content: The dense microstructure and barrier phases at 1000 °C result in the best oxidation resistance.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The sample sintered at 1000 °C (LW1000) exhibits the most outstanding oxidation resistance due to its dense microstructure and uniformly distributed barrier phases that effectively impede diffusion.

mechanism_principle.content: High work-hardening rate and coexistence of ductile and hard phases hinder further refinement.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This can be attributed to the high work-hardening rate of the high-entropy alloy system, as well as the coexistence of ductile components (e.g., Al, Fe) and hard phases

mechanism_principle.content: High temperature and pressure provide high diffusion activity to promote oxide growth.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This is attributed to the fact that, within the severe lattice distortion characteristic of high-entropy alloys, sufficiently high temperature and sintering pressure provide atoms with extremely high diffusion activity

mechanism_principle.content: A dense passive film blocks Cl- ions, shifting corrosion from direct attack to penetration-defense mode.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This dense passive film (high R f ) effectively blocks the uniform penetration of aggressive Cl − ions, confining corrosion to local weak points in the film.

hypothesis_statement.content: The study employs mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering to fabricate a novel alloy and investigates the effects of sintering temperature, aiming to provide evidence for developing high-performance alloys.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: To address these challenges, this study employs mechanical alloying (MA)—a method capable of extending solid solubility and suppressing intermetallic compound formation [ [16] ]—combined with spark plasma sintering (SPS) to fabricate a novel six-component MgAlTiVFeCo lightweight high-entropy alloy. The effects of sintering temperature on the phase composition, microstructure, densification behavior, microhardness, high-temperature oxidation resistance, and corrosion resistance of the alloy are systematically investigated. This work aims to provide experimental evidence and theoretical reference for developing high-performance lightweight high-entropy alloys through composition and process design

hypothesis_statement.content: High-temperature sintering promotes property optimization by achieving a favorable microstructure.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: At 1000 °C, a microstructure most conducive to property optimization is achieved.

evidence_result.content: Corrosion resistance improved at high temperatures, evidenced by more positive potential and lower current density at 1000 °C.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Compared to alloys sintered at medium-to-low temperatures (850–950 °C), the alloy sintered at a high temperature (1000 °C) exhibits a more positive corrosion potential (−0.438 V) and a lower corrosion current density (1.07 × 10 −6 A·cm −2 )

evidence_result.content: 1000 °C identified as the optimal sintering temperature demonstrating superior comprehensive properties.
evidence_result.evidence_span: It is evident that 1000 °C is the optimal sintering temperature, and the MgAlTiVFeCo LW-HEA demonstrates superior comprehensive properties.

evidence_result.content: After 100 h of milling, a single BCC solid solution phase was formed.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Finally, after 100 h of milling, all other peaks disappeared, and a single BCC solid solution phase was formed.

evidence_result.content: Crystallite size decreases as milling time increases.
evidence_result.evidence_span: As the milling time increases, the crystallite size gradually decreases.

evidence_result.content: Microstrain and grain refinement coexist in powders milled for 100 h.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The results indicate that both significant grain refinement and microstrain coexist in the powders

evidence_result.content: Sintering temperature influences phase precipitation, with some oxides forming only at high temperatures.
evidence_result.evidence_span: However, when the sintering temperature rises to 1000 °C, phases such as AlV 2 O 4 , FeAl 2 O 4 , and FeTiO 3 precipitate.

evidence_result.content: LW1000 exhibits the lowest corrosion rate and best corrosion resistance.
evidence_result.evidence_span: These observations demonstrate that LW1000 exhibits the lowest corrosion rate and the best corrosion resistance

evidence_result.content: Relative density and microhardness increase synergistically with sintering temperature, peaking at 1000 °C.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Both the relative density and microhardness of the alloy exhibit a synergistic increasing trend with rising sintering temperature. Sintering at 1000 °C achieves a combination of high relative density (96.7%) and high hardness (1235.5 HV).

constraint.content: Sintering temperature must be limited to 1000 °C to avoid magnesium volatilization which causes composition deviations.
constraint.evidence_span: To avoid composition and property deviations caused by the loss of principal elements, the maximum sintering temperature was limited to 1000 °C.

constraint.content: Sintering temperature must be above 800 °C because lower temperatures result in insufficient driving force and low relative density (<80%).
constraint.evidence_span: when the SPS temperature was lower than 800 °C, the sintering driving force was insufficient, resulting in compacts with very low relative density (<80%) that could not form bulk materials with structural integrity or be suitable for performance testing.

constraint.content: The alloy meets the design criterion for lightweight materials with density below 6 g/cm3.
constraint.evidence_span: The calculated theoretical density of the MgAlTiVFeCo high-entropy alloy is 5.304 g/cm 3 , which meets the design criterion for lightweight high-entropy alloys (density < 6 g/cm 3 ).
